title: The real question: what 'grace' means in the texts on salvation
source_text: XLVIII. Id vero solum in quaestione est, An in illis scripturae locis ubi dicimur per Dei gratiam servari & justificari, gratia significet externum Dei favorem & benevolentiam: an vero gratiam aliquam quae nobis inhaereat, seu actualis illa sit, sive habitualis. Prius affirmat Schola Reformata, posterius Romana.
pass_a_gloss: XLVIII. But this only is in question, Whether in those places of scripture where we are said to be saved and justified by the grace of God, grace signifies the external favour and benevolence of God: or some grace which inheres in us, whether that be actual, or habitual. The former the Reformed School affirms, the latter the Roman.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLVIII. The only point in question is this. In the passages of scripture that say we are saved and justified by God's grace, does grace mean God's external favour and goodwill, or some grace that inheres in us, whether actual or habitual?
The Reformed school affirms the first, the Roman school the second.
